experiment: Seventeen single-span, two-purlin-line standing seam roof assemblies (Z- and C-purlins with rib or pan panels, sliding or fixed clips, with and without blanket insulation, at 20, 25 and 30 ft spans) were loaded to failure by gravity (vacuum chamber) pressure, and tensile coupons were cut from the web of each failed purlin.
title: Base Test Method for Gravity Loaded Standing Seam Roof Systems

variables.definition: Alphanumeric label encoding deck type, clip type, purlin depth/shape/thickness, span and flange orientation for each base test.
variables.evidence: Table 3.1 p.16; Tables 4.1-4.5 pp.27-34; Table S1
variables.name: Test identification
variables.note: Several designations are printed inconsistently between tables; preserved verbatim.

variables.definition: Test series (I through IV) grouping configurations by purlin shape, orientation, deck/clip system and span, as printed in table body headings.
variables.evidence: Table 3.1 p.16 and Table 4.5 p.34 (series heading rows moved into a leading column)
variables.name: Test series

variables.definition: Cross-sectional shape of the supporting purlins, C- or Z-section.
variables.name: Purlin cross-section shape

variables.definition: Whether the two purlin lines have their top flanges opposed (pointing in opposite directions) or facing the same direction.
variables.name: Purlin flange orientation

variables.definition: Standing seam deck panel configuration used, Rib or Pan type (Fig. 3.1).
variables.name: Panel (deck) type

variables.definition: Type of standing seam clip connecting panel to purlin, sliding (two-piece) or fixed (Fig. 3.2).
variables.name: Clip type

variables.definition: Whether 4 in. blanket insulation was placed between the purlin top flange and the clip/panel during the test (Yes/No).
variables.name: Insulation present
variables.note: Insulation thickness of 4 in. is stated in the column definition, not as a separate column.

variables.definition: Simple span length of the single-span base test, printed in feet and inches (20, 25 or 30 ft; one test at 24'-9").
variables.evidence: Table 3.1 p.16 (span_length); Table S1 (span_ft); footnote * in Tables 4.1 and 4.5
variables.name: Span length
variables.note: One Series I test span printed as 24'-9" because purlins were cut 3 in. short.

variables.definition: Nominal depth of the purlin section taken from the test designation.
variables.name: Nominal purlin depth

variables.definition: Nominal purlin base-metal thickness implied by the test designation.
variables.name: Nominal purlin thickness
variables.note: Differs in several cases from the measured coupon thickness in Table 4.5.

variables.definition: Measured thickness of the tensile coupon cut from the web of the failed purlin.
variables.name: Measured coupon thickness
variables.note: Printed values sometimes differ from the thickness in the test label; preserved verbatim.

variables.definition: Yield stress determined by the 0.2% offset method from a tensile coupon taken from the web of the purlin that failed.
variables.name: Yield stress

variables.definition: Ultimate tensile strength of the coupon cut from the failed purlin web.
variables.name: Tensile strength

variables.definition: Percent elongation measured in the tensile coupon test.
variables.name: Coupon elongation

variables.definition: Effective section modulus of the purlin that failed, computed per AISI effective-width procedures.
variables.name: Effective section modulus

variables.definition: Nominal flexural section strength computed as the product of the effective section modulus and the measured yield stress.
variables.name: Nominal section strength
variables.note: Columns headed Mn while legend of Table 4.1 labels it differently; preserved as printed.

variables.definition: Maximum bending moment corresponding to the experimental failure load of the base test, with no factor of safety applied.
variables.name: Experimental failure moment
variables.note: Some table legends define Wus/WAISI (loads) while columns are headed Mus; preserved as printed.

variables.definition: Experimental ultimate uniform load per purlin line at failure, obtained from the vacuum chamber pressure and including the system dead load.
variables.evidence: Table S1 failure_load_as_printed, from Appendix test summary sheets (pp. 47-130)
variables.name: Experimental failure load
variables.note: Reported per purlin line with 5 ft tributary width.

variables.definition: Fully constrained (through-fastened) bending failure load per purlin line predicted by the 1986 AISI Specification and printed on each appendix test summary sheet.
variables.name: Predicted constrained failure load

variables.definition: Experimental failure moment expressed as a percentage of the 1986 AISI fully constrained (through-fastened) flexural capacity, R = Mus/MAISI x 100.
variables.name: Percent of through-fastened capacity

variables.definition: Fully constrained through-fastened flexural capacity per the 1986 AISI Specification, used as the denominator of R but not tabulated directly.
variables.evidence: Legend of Tables 4.1-4.4 and Table S1 note defining R = Mus/M_AISI x 100%
variables.name: AISI constrained moment capacity

variables.definition: Observed mode of failure, LB = local buckling of lip, flange and web, LM = failure of cross section after considerable lateral movement.
variables.name: Failure mode
variables.note: Appendix summary sheets report LM as 'Lateral Buckling'.

variables.definition: Direction of the applied load; all tests were gravity (positive moment) vacuum-chamber loading with no uplift tests.
variables.evidence: Table S1 load_direction and header note
variables.name: Load direction

variables.definition: Number of spans in the test assembly; all tests were single span, simply supported.
variables.name: Number of spans

variables.definition: Number of parallel purlin lines in the test assembly (two for all base tests).
variables.name: Number of purlin lines

variables.definition: Lateral bracing condition of the purlins; all tests were braced at the supports only.
variables.name: Lateral bracing condition

variables.definition: Center-to-center spacing of the two purlin lines, equal to the tributary width used to convert pressure to line load, stated as 5 ft for all tests.
variables.evidence: Table S1 header notes: 'purlin lines spaced 5 ft. on center' and 'Tributary width per purlin line is 5 ft.'
variables.name: Purlin spacing / tributary width
variables.note: Single value for all tests; not a column.

variables.definition: Width of deck cantilevering beyond each exterior purlin web, 1 ft for all tests.
variables.evidence: Table S1 header note: '1 ft. deck overhang beyond each purlin web'
variables.name: Deck overhang
variables.note: Single value for all tests; not a column.

variables.definition: System dead load per purlin line included in the reported failure loads, stated on individual test summary sheets as 7.1 to 9.74 plf.
variables.evidence: Table S1 header note on failure loads
variables.name: System dead load
variables.note: Range only; individual values on appendix pages.
